raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, and I am 65 years old, so I will keep my wheat-maize rotation simple, steady, and manageable by myself. I have done this for many years, and with well irrigation I will rely on the usual pattern that is familiar and low-risk for me. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer at planting, give a few irrigations at key stages, and keep pesticide use limited but not zero because I do not want yield loss from disease or insects. For maize, I will choose hybrid seed because I care about stable production on small land, use a bit more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate in the important growth stages, and keep field work practical with rotary tillage. I will not push for the highest possible input level, because at my age and farm size I would rather aim for stable yield, manageable labor, and dependable grain output from both seasons.
